page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.tiny is an entry-level virtual server configuration within the shared family. It features a single vCPU mapped to one physical core on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance includes 1.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:1 ratio of memory to compute core. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included, and the instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring attached network block storage for persistent data operations.

Performance across synthetic benchmarks reflects the constrained capacity of a single-core, low-memory footprint. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core CPU score reached 1087.59, ranking in the bottom quartile of evaluated systems, while the overall PassMark CPU score registered at 1316.17. Memory subsystems demonstrated large-block uncached read throughput of 8.5 GB/s and write throughput of 7.1 GB/s. Application tests measured static web serving throughput at 0.93 GB/s and Redis SET operations at 1.43 million operations per second.

Due to its minimal resource allocation, the ecs.n1.tiny offers low resource overhead and minimal operational cost within the entry-tier classification. However, the trade-off includes limited memory capacity and compute headroom, which constrain concurrent task processing and memory-intensive applications.

This server instance is best suited for lightweight utility workloads, low-traffic internal test servers, lightweight microservices, and simple bastion or jump hosts where memory and compute requirements remain minimal.

Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it is configured with 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1.0 GB of memory. The instance has no integrated local storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate entry-level capabilities, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 1316.17 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1087.59. Memory bandwidth reaches 8.5 GB/s on large read operations, and static web serving throughput measures 0.93 GB/s. With low resource consumption and dedicated core mapping, it represents a cost-effective choice for small-footprint environments. The ecs.n1.tiny is appropriate for low-traffic web proxies, jump hosts, development sandboxes, and basic background tasks that operate within tight memory constraints.
